utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, the Status Conference. Does counsel for either accused wish to raise any matter under Rule 65 bis for the Trial Chamber's consideration. Mr. Ackerman, you're first on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have nothing to raise with regard to the Status Conference this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. De Roux. MR. DE ROUX: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We would like to have clarification for several points with the Prosecution. We had a conversation this morning which may allow us to make some proposals in respect of the holding of the trial. The Prosecution told us this morning that the disclosure of documents that we've been asking for for some time now would be carried out for us and the documents could be disclosed going all the way to the month of December. I believe that's what they said. That means in principle that at the end of the year, we would have the Prosecution's documents and would be in a position to study them and to answer them within a time period covering about six months which might allow us to set a date for the trial and to set that date today, if the Chamber agrees, because today General Talic has been in prison now for 11 months and it seems natural that in front of this Tribunal, as in front of any jurisdiction, a detainee should be able to be tried within reasonable time periods. And referring, for example, to the Strasbourg Court of Human Rights, in respect of a reasonable time period, which might go over two years for a detained person, I think that that is the case law which has been accepted internationally and that this is a figure relating to rights of people today. Therefore, it is clear that we would like now, as quickly as possible after having set the rules for disclosure with the Prosecution, the disclosure of documents, I think that that was to a very large extent settled this morning, we would like to be able to determine a date for the trial within the time limits that are generally accepted. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Pitron, do you want to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Well, now, Ms. Korner, one thing that we did reserve for today from the motion for disclosure of evidence was to fix a time limit under Rule 66(A)(ii). So that's one thing we have to do. Are you able to give us a date that you will be able to comply with that Rule?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of all the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Those are all -- 66(A)(ii), the statements of all the witnesses, affidavits, formal statements, et cetera, of your witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The answer is I can't -- effectively I can't at this stage say when that will be completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, is this going to be held up in some box somewhere upstairs until you've got them all ready, or can they be sent progressively so that counsel for the Defence can start reading them?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They're going to be sent progressively. Can I say that the reason that further statements outside the sets disclosed for the amended indictment haven't been is because we were waiting for the ruling on protective measures. We do have other statements that we will be disclosing within the very near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, if it's going to be a progressive one, I'm not sure how I can formulate an order. But I think that there should be some way in which the Tribunal can enforce it in case you start to fall behind. How many have you got that you've got to disclose?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the moment, I couldn't -- I couldn't really give Your Honours a figure. We have been accumulating statements over the period which, as I say, the only reason they haven't been disclosed so far is because of the order. Would Your Honour give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told helpfully by my friends that something in the region of 30 to 40 we will be disclosing in the very near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, let's fix a date for those. The end of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the holiday season, and we have to contact the various witnesses still to find out about their fears and whatever, would Your Honours say the second week in September?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Who is on holiday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The witnesses may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, they may be.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This was asked for by Mr. Talic in a motion filed on the 5th of June, and on the 27th of June we said this can be dealt with at the Status Conference on the 20th of July. I must say I would have expected the Prosecution to be a little bit more ready to comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say that one of the -- the difficulties we've had. Your Honours have issued the ruling in the protective measures some, what is it, two days -- the 3rd of July. Since then, as Your Honours know, we've been chasing after the witnesses we have already disclosed to establish what the situation is. We haven't had the opportunity to chase after the witnesses that we haven't disclosed yet. That's been the problem. As Your Honours saw and the Defence have seen, we have a real manpower problem in the sense that the investigative team is dealing with three cases, one of which is presently in trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the teams are not one person. There must be somebody who can start doing this work. We may not be in trial at the moment but the Defence is entitled to know and to have them in good time to start reading them. So I really feel that we've got to do a bit better than just the second week of September. That's seven weeks away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In that case, would Your Honours say -- I haven't got a calendar on me at the moment but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was going to say the 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not seeking to dissuade Your Honour from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that mean that we'll only have 40 documents served by the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How many? I think we've got to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can't tell Your Honours because it may be that we'll be seeking protective measures in which case we'll have to file a motion on Your Honours' ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well that's a matter which we have to deal with because you have asked for an extension of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I hope that I have understood this correctly. Your Honours' ruling at present dealt with the witnesses disclosed but redacted. Future witnesses, if we wish to obtain protective measures, we will have to file a motion in respect of each witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well one would imagine one motion dealing with a lot at a time, just as you do when you are bringing your witnesses along for trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not something which is new or extraordinary. It's well-known in the procedures of the Tribunal, and it's been applied, so far as I know, in every case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It was your move in redacting everything which seemed to be new.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought we'd passed that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You did ask for that, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Accepting that, Your Honour, we will serve -- sorry, disclose such witnesses as we do not seek protective measures for in the sense of withholding the name until a later date by the date Your Honour has given, the 31st. How many that will be, I cannot say, but it will be a reasonably substantial number. But I would ask that Your Honours don't say that we have to serve -- disclose 30 statements by that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You do say in your request for an extension of time, you don't understand whether redact includes a reference to the address.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: An unredacted document, the word "redact" is reasonably unknown in the English language, but if you take it as meaning obliterating something, then an unredacted document must be something in which there are no obliterations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well, that's the reason we raised it. First of all, I want to be clear that we're not required by the terms of Your Honours' order to give to the Defence the current addresses of any witnesses who've happened to move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No. You are required only to give the statements. If you want to get a redaction of their address, which may be reasonable, I think, for the Defence really to show why they needed it -- they may need it, for example, because there's more than one person with that name so there may have to be some better identification given -- but you have to only give the statements at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whatever address is on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you want to get that redacted, then you should apply for a redaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, thank you, that does help. Could I also ask whether Your Honours are granting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was going to ask whether there was any objection. It was a week's extension, as I recall. Is there any objection to the extension of time which the Prosecution seeks of a week?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. As much as I've been waiting for over a year, a week isn't going to make much difference to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's what I would have hoped that you'd say, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Pitron.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to make some comments in order to make things more clear because I think that things are getting a bit confused. It seems that the Prosecutor is mixing up several problems. First, I would like to make a preliminary comment. General Talic has been in prison for 11 months. I had dared to think, and I've been daring to think for the past 11 months, that the Prosecution knew which documents it was basing its accusations against my client on. I'm shocked to see that even today, if I've understood correctly what's been said, several weeks are still needed, if not several months, before the Prosecution itself knows which documents it's basing its charges on. These preliminary comments now having been made, I would like to make three additional observations. We have the first problem which has to do with disclosure of the documents which the Prosecution has in order to support its charges. Without wanting to break any confidentiality, we had a conversation with Ms. Korner and Ms. Erasmus out of which I understood that the Prosecutor was in a position to submit to us by the 4th of August three diskettes which represent approximately 40 binders of documents which corresponded to the essential things in these documents. The proposal was made in writing by the Prosecutor and we agreed to it. The Prosecutor has then told us that until the end of the year -- or at the end of the year, she would be in a position to have given us to or disclose to us all of the documents that are going to support the charges, and we agreed to that time period; although once again we needed 16 months for the Prosecution to give to us all the documents that it has against our client since the beginning of this case. In order to finish with this first comment, I would like to go back to what Xavier De Roux said: We are in a position, since we know the date that the Prosecutor is to disclose the evidence, to set the schedule for the trial, and it seems to me that the date could be set for the trial to begin. We have a second point which is different, and that has to do with confidentiality of the documents that have already been disclosed by the Prosecution or which will be so disclosed. On this point as well, the Prosecutor has written that she was asking until the 31st of July in order to comply with the Tribunal's decision, that is, to respect the complete adversarial system in respect of these documents that are being disclosed, except for perhaps some. We agreed to that date of the 31st of July. We are merely asking, but I think that here, too, there was an agreement with the Prosecutor, we are merely asking that this unconfidentiality [sic] be understood and extended not only to those documents which have been disclosed by the Prosecutor with the indictment, as has been mentioned in the Tribunal's orders, but that making these documents not confidential should be extended to all of the documents that are disclosed by the Prosecution, which appears to me very logical. Lastly, there is a final point, if I've understood the Prosecutor correctly, she is asking -- as part of this making documents not confidential, she wishes to keep back the witnesses' addresses. I do not see in any of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence that that reservation is provided for. There is merely a reservation having to do with the names of the witnesses and that in exceptional cases the addresses as well. Only in those exceptional cases, duly justified by the Prosecution to Your Honours, would you be in a position, Your Honours, to agree to maintain confidentiality. I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think the confusion may be the way we've been discussing it without reference to the orders that were made. The orders which were made were that the Prosecution was, by the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 24th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- yes, 24th of July, 4.00 p.m., to serve or to produce all of the material, supporting material which accompanied the indictment in its unredacted form unless there was a motion made within that period for protective orders in relation to particular victims or witnesses. It's that particular time limit, the 24th of July, that an application has been made for an extension to the 31st of July. Now, as I understand it, both accused have accepted that, so that order is therefore made. What we have been discussing apart from that are the documents referred to in Rule 66(A)(ii) which deal with documents beyond the supporting material, and they're described as the statements of all witnesses whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at trial, or affidavits or formal statements of those witnesses. Now, it's in relation to those particular documents that we've been discussing more generally the date, the 31st of August, and that is where, I think, perhaps, Mr. Pitron, you have confused the matter. Now, in relation to the order which Mr. Talic had sought in a previous motion was to have a time limit set under that particular Rule. Now, the way in which I think we can describe it is that all witness statements for which there will be no application made for protective orders will be supplied by the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, August, yes. The 31st of August. I'm sorry. The application in relation to those documents, when will you be able to get that on? That's the application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of witnesses to be served before the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we're seeking protective measures, we will have the motion in the week before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, by that date would do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or by that date, if Your Honour says by that date. Your Honour, what Mr. Pitron, or what both Defence counsel for General Talic asked for was complete disclosure of every witness that's going to be called or every piece of documentation. Your Honour is not ruling that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No. They may get it, I don't know, but you have a right to make an application for protective orders. If you succeed, then they won't get it; if you don't succeed, they will get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, but what they're going to -- may I make it -- can I roll back, as it were, make it absolutely clear. We are following the letter of the motion. Each witness has been contacted and been asked the questions in respect of protective measures. If they are content or have no good reason for asking for protective measures, then the Defence will get the completely unredacted version of the statements. What I'm concerned about is that Your Honour is not ruling -- isn't saying that for the purposes of trial, every witness on which the Prosecution intends to rely at trial must be served by the 31st of August, because that's what Defence counsel asked in that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It means every statement, and I'll refer to them generically as a statement, every statement within Rule 66(A)(ii) for which you are not seeking protective measures must be served by the 31st of August. In relation to those for which you do seek protective measures, the motion must be filed by that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But, you see, if you look at Rule 66(A)(ii), Your Honour, it says: "... copies of the statements of all witnesses whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at trial."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see the difficulty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you have that intention, you must serve them. If you form an intention later to call other ones, then we will have to deal with them when that intention is formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we better make this absolutely clear. We have statements from certain witnesses, but other witnesses are still in the process of being interviewed and statements taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you haven't yet formed an intention to call them at the trial; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, that must be right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If that's so, you don't have to disclose them at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think anybody who's had anything to do with any criminal litigation would realise that these are ongoing preparations on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And that the Prosecution isn't obliged to have everything in writing and all of its intentions formed at the time that it issues or seeks to have the indictment confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, in that case we will comply with Your Honours' order that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. But if you do form an intention to call others, then we would expect you to notify the accused and to provide them with the copies in accordance with that Rule as soon as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely. That is our intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But at each Status Conference, you will be asked, "Have you formed an intention to call any other witnesses," just as you will be asked at every Status Conference whether there are any documents within Rule 68 that you can disclose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, that, of course, is a matter which will no doubt arise in relation to the latest motion we've had from Mr. Talic, the one for which the English version was filed two days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't expect you to discuss that here because you haven't had an opportunity to put a response on but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I say straight away, as I understand it, it's an application to the Registry for confidential documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't have anything to do with us, as I read the English translation. I think they're asking Your Honours, as I read it, and I'm sure that Mr. Pitron will tell me if I'm wrong, they're asking Your Honours to order the Registry to disclose documentation relating to previous trials at this Tribunal. MR. DE ROUX: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. I've got it here. The Defence has requested the Registry, and I would think that the Registry would have to seek your views before anything was done. The Registry is going to say there's an order that these documents be kept confidential, and there will be no way in which the Registrar can disclose them without an order from the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: On which I would think the Prosecution would have to state its views.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll consider the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's why I say it's really rather pointless trying to discuss it here when we both only just got the document. Now, Mr. Pitron, you wanted to say something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Perhaps two comments in order to make things clearer. The first comment has to do with the last request of ours, if we're speaking about the same thing, that is, the request in which we are asking the Registry to give to us certain documents which were used in four cases that the Tribunal has already heard or which are being heard at this Tribunal. We also asked the Registry to provide to us all documents that are public as well as several which are confidential. We asked the Tribunal to authorise us to have access to those confidential documents. It seems to me that this falls within the jurisdiction of this Trial Chamber, and I have difficulty seeing how the Prosecutor, who had access to those documents because it was part of the trials and can use them in its case, I don't see how the Prosecutor could object to those confidential documents being transmitted to the Defence of General Talic. It's being understood that we will respect the fact that these documents are confidential, and we commit ourselves to doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may be right. I really don't want to have this particular motion debated here. I think the problem that arose was whether it was going to come before the Trial Chamber at all. I agree with you, it would be within the jurisdiction of this Trial Chamber to determine anything which relates to this Trial Chamber. The two matters before Trial Chamber III, there may have to be an application made to Trial Chamber III. I don't decide that one way or the other. But it may be that we have no jurisdiction to vary a ruling made by that Trial Chamber that documents are to be kept as confidential documents. Let's worry about that one when the Prosecution has had an opportunity to consider it and to put a response on, and we will certainly invite the Registrar to put a response on as well so that we have the matter firmly in our view. Mr. Ackerman is rising, I think, to ask whether he can have access to them as well. Is that what you're rising for you, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, can we deal with one thing at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assumed that we had concluded this issue about these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, we have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: As soon as we do that, I will then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I go back to a matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can I say we should leave that motion, the most recent motion, to take its ordinary course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But I would expect the Prosecution will be asked to put on a response, and that's why -- I think we've at least cleared that much up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And we will invite the Registrar also, under the Rules, to put on a response as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pitron, is there anything more you want to say about what we are dealing with, or are you still talking about this new motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm staying within the scope of this discussion. I'm answering Ms. Korner who just asked what it is we had agreed about this morning. So I come back to you with this very important question, at least I feel it's very important, that is, the disclosure of documents of the Prosecution. That's what I'm talking about. If I've understood you correctly, Your Honour, you said to us that Ms. Korner is going to disclose to us by the 31st of August those documents that she has. If in the future she has other documents, she will disclose them in the future. At the next Status Conference, you will ask her whether she has any other documents and you will evaluate what new time periods are required for the latest requests for disclosure of documents that she may present at that time. I would like, with all due respect to you, to draw your attention to the fact that this means for me that the Prosecution still has an unlimited time for disclosing in a progressive way those documents which make my client's detention a reality for the past 11 months. With all respect, I ask the Tribunal to, once and for all, set a time limit for the Prosecution for all of the documents to be disclosed to me which are the basis for the accusations, knowing that at 2.00, the Prosecutor will say that the end of December 2000 seems to her to be a proper date for this matter and that we agreed to that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner, there are two things which Mr. Pitron has referred to that I wanted to ask you. First, what is this that you are disclosing by the 4th of August, the three diskettes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I've been trying rather desperately to get to that part. What happened is that we had an application originally from Mr. Ackerman on behalf of Brdjanin for all the documents that were seized from the Banja Luka municipality. We wrote to Defence counsel for General Talic saying that we were going to accede to that request made under Rule 66(B), that they wish to make the same request, and they did. The documents have been burnt, if that's the correct expression, onto CDs and the intention was to disclose today, to both sets of Defence counsel, those CDs. Regrettably, something technically arose late yesterday which means that they will have to be redone but they will be available, and we have undertaken that they will be given to the Defence by the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can I just clear something up so we can get all the orders straight. Those documents have been disclosed under Rule 68 or merely under 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Under 66(B). The Defence made a request for documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In effect, what they're getting is, with one exception, the totality of the documents seized from the Banja Luka municipality which include, and that is of the greatest interest to Mr. Pitron and Mr. De Roux, the documents taken from the headquarters of the 1st Krajina Corps of which General Talic was the commanding officer during the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Now, they will be supplied by the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They will be supplied by the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, what is it -- I'm sorry, yes. Something more you want to add to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That will provide the Defence with the bulk of the documents, all of them, that is to say, those that the Prosecution intends to use to prove the case and those which fall possibly under the auspices of Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that we better get that cleared up. Are you supplying all the documents that were seized from the Banja Luka municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: With one exception; those taken from what's called the CSB, the police station. Those, we will continue, for the moment -- it may well be at a later stage we'll be able to provide those on CD as well, but those for the moment will be disclosed under the normal procedures, i.e., under Rule 66, although it only talks about statements, and Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Were they part of the request?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We were just asked to supply the Banja Luka municipal buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that where the CSB is?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. It's a separate area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then, we'll have a formal order drawn up later on. But we will make an order that you supply on CDs copies of the documents seized from the Banja Luka municipality, 1st Krajina Corps, by the 4th of August, pursuant to Rule 66(B).

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It's a request which we're complying with. I don't think it needs an order from Your Honours but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think it might be preferable that we made one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I see that Mr. De Roux is on his feet. Can I just finish for one moment? And Mr. Ackerman. Can I just finish?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll come to you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of the CDs, we are asking Your Honour to make an order that these be returned to the Prosecution at the conclusion of the proceedings against the two defendants. It is not in the same category as the materials we discussed on the last occasion, because clearly anything that the Defence wishes to use it will print out from the CDs. These documents seized eventually will have to be returned to the municipality. They were seized on an order from this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But as I understand it, what you are providing are copies of those documents on CDs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In electronic format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the electronic format we wish to have returned, and I don't think -- I've spoken to both Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Pitron about that, there is no objection to that order. But Your Honour can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if it's by consent, there can be no trouble. Now, Mr. De Roux, who was on his feet first. Yes. MR. DE ROUX: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to add a clarification because there would be an order. The letter of the Prosecutor from the 28th of June states clearly that the documents, which will be disclosed to us, are those that were seized in 1998. We have just said this, that it was in the municipality of Banja Luka, but they were also at a radio station in Banja Luka, at the offices of the SDS party, and at the 1st Army Corps. These are the seizures that were made in four different locations, and those are the documents that are suggested are being disclosed to us in electronic form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if we're going to have this sort of dispute, I'm going to leave it to the parties to sort out. I'm not going to try and resolve this. Either you go into the witness box, either of you, and give us evidence under oath -- just a moment, please, Mr. Ackerman -- or you sort it out between yours. If you can't, then there will have to be a specific application made about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think we need to trouble Your Honours. It is not a matter that Your Honours need to make a ruling on. It's an application under Rule 66(B) which we have acceded to. The only problem has been a technical one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's just that there is a disagreement between you as to what you're going to produce. You've said you are not producing, at this stage, the documents seized from the police and CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is no dispute, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They're getting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry, but Mr. De Roux is expecting not only the documents seized from the Banja Luka municipality but also those from the CSB, from the radio station, and from the SDS party. Now, I just don't want to have to worry about that here. If you can't work it out between yourselves, then you'll have to put an application on and we'll deal with it. I would hope that common sense will dictate, that it will be resolved between you, and I'm not going to have it done here in court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Can I say there is no dispute. Mr. De Roux has written and he knows it's not the CSB because we discussed it. I think there's a confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, the other question I have to ask you which has been raised by Mr. Pitron was something that was going to be supplied by the end of the year. Now, what is it that you say is going to be supplied by the end of the year?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. May I say I have some difficulties with what was discussed in the private meeting and raised in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If it doesn't relate to the documents that are in issue here under 66(A) --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It does not relate to the statements. The request that was raised this morning that's been raised is this: We were asked when is it that you can disclose all the documents on which you rely against General Talic? I explained to Defence counsel -- Mr. Ackerman regrettably couldn't be there, I hope to have had a general meeting but he couldn't -- that as was explained to a court yesterday, that because of the huge quantities of documents in this institution, to comply with our obligations, particularly under Rule 68(A), a huge search project was going on, and that it would take until November to be completed and therefore we could not say that we would be in a position to satisfy our obligations before Christmas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But are we perfectly clear that you will be complying with your obligations under 66(A)(ii) by the 31st of August, or in relation to those you seek protective measures for, you will have a motion on by the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, provided that Your Honour is not reading Rule 66(A)(ii) as saying that anybody that we wish to call at trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no, look, the Rule is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at trial. Now, if there is no present intention, you have no obligation to disclose it unless it falls within, say, 68. So let us not worry about interpretations. It's very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But I will repeat: The Trial Chamber would expect you, the Prosecution, to reveal any intention that you do form when you form it and produce the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And I don't want that to have to wait until each Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My reference to you being asked at a Status Conference is that usually there is a question asked by Rule 66 and 68 at each Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have that perfectly in mind. We will be disclosing, as soon as we form the intention, to call a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Now, Mr. Ackerman, you've been trying very hard to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I started this whole mess and so I'd like to explain to the Chamber what I was attempting to do. What I was trying to do with my communications with Ms. Korner regarding documents was to avoid getting the Trial Chamber involved in this piecemeal process of discovery as we went along, thinking that we could probably accomplish it between Ms. Korner and I, without bothering the Trial Chamber about it, and I still believe that's the case. My view of the issue that's come up this morning is this: If Ms. Korner tells me that there are, her word, "millions of documents in the Tribunal in their office," and they don't know, at this point, which of them may be relevant to this case and which of them may be exculpatory with regard to this case and that there is this search that's going on that she tells me, and told you now, may take until the end of November. I am unwilling, at this point, to ask the Trial Chamber to place any kind of deadline upon the Prosecution with regard to that process, because it's important to me that they not hurry through that process and therefore miss something that could be exculpatory to my client and that they would have to disclose to me. So I'm very comfortable with having the Prosecutor proceed at their pace regarding going through these documents and being very careful about it and disclosing to us, progressively, in piecemeal, as they go along what they find. Now, if that process can end by the end of December, so be it. If it cannot end until the end of January, so be it. There's a point, I suppose, when the Chamber would want to impose an absolute deadline upon that process, but I think we can accept in the good faith representation of Ms. Korner that it appears to her that that can end around December. Also, based upon those representations, there is no way that any of us can tell you at this point what the quantity of documents that will result from that search process are going to be. That, therefore, makes it very difficult to say, if we get these documents at the end of December, we will be ready to go to trial on such and such a date, because whether I'm ready to go to trial or not depends on how long it will take me to go through those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let me say here and now we are not going to fix a date for the trial. There is another trial to be disposed of by Trial Chamber II before we reach this one, and it may be that another Trial Chamber will become free and it will take this one in its place. But until the matter is ready for trial, there will be no trial dates fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I had to say. I intend, unless I'm told by the Trial Chamber, at least on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin, to continue trying to accomplish these discovery matters on an informal basis with Ms. Korner rather than troubling the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well I would hope so too. I would hope that both defendants will proceed upon that basis and that each camp, as it were, will read the material as it comes rather than waiting until it's all there and then say we need five months or six months to read it. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I confirm that you've made an order of the return of the CDs at the end of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to make orders about that because we will make one when you have agreed as to what's going to be produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But even though, Your Honour, can I tell Your Honour there is no disagreement but it is important that before -- because Your Honours might be seized of the matter on the 4th of August -- before we hand it over, that there really isn't any doubt that the CDs must come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's only because it's by consent. If it's not the original documents, I'm not quite sure what the problem is, because they could make a copy of the CD. Is it because of the cost of the CDs you're worried about, the four CDs?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not the cost. We would hope -- Your Honour said that they would copy the CDs. I would hope they wouldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You said that they could print out the documents from it what we're concerned about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not the same. What we're concerned about, Your Honour, I would hope Your Honour is aware as well, is that there aren't CDs containing documents floating around the place, because they're not documents that belong to this Tribunal that, if you like, are [inaudible] on them while the case go on. But they belong to the municipality and the various other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The CDs do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The CDs belong to us, the Office of the Prosecutor. We are giving the Defence those CDs, enabling them to print documents off, but we would like an order that the CDs be returned to the Office of the Prosecutor at the conclusion of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are they your only copy?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, as I say, it's by consent. But otherwise, I must say, Ms. Korner, I wouldn't have made the order because this is going back to this argument we had on the protective measures as to who owns the documents handed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are not documents. These are an electronic means of getting access to the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be no different than having photographs, would it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, as I say, it's by consent. So an order will be made that any CDs by which copies of documents have been supplied to the Defence must be returned at the end of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But it is also understood by everybody that copies of the documents encrypted on the CDs may be made and kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there anything else? Then I'm very grateful to counsel for their assistance, and the matter is adjourned.
